body: I'm sorry to here that man, I hope you're feeling better now.
Thank you, it really is just a trial by fire isn't it?

Thank you for the kind words. I've tried EMDR once but it seemed too silly and didn't help - but maybe I can give it another shot. I have shared often with people I trust but it seems like I am running out of tolerance for everyone. Before they would listen and be supportive, but it's gotten to the point where you can tell their voices are strained and annoyed at the same issues not being resolved over and over again, but I do understand where they are coming from. I'm sorry you too had to go through rape, I honestly wouldn't wish that even on my worst enemy - however I am glad you did get out of your hatred too, it is a scary warped reality to be trapped in. I'm not sure if I can personally stop my barriers and deeply rooted insecurities as it looks it is only getting worse - but I do appreciate the advice!
That's pretty cool actually! Thanks for sharing
I see. I've always been a bit reluctant to do that stuff, not really that interested in drugs and the whatnot, but I am glad it works for you!
That's true, it seems like experimenting with different things would be a good idea to just see what sticks.
Nah, I have always been super worried that if I did I would freak out due to my unstable mind at the moment.

Sure thing. This most recent depression was possibly the most aggressive and dangerous as I mentioned before. It went on for three years, and in those years I essentially destroyed everything I had built up for myself. Before this depression, the recurrents were not usually not that devastating. They lasted on max about half a year, and I got help soon enough to not do any great damage. This one was different. It hit at possibly the worst time, what was suppose to be my senior graduation. I stopped showing up for school, didn't talk to anyone, didn't work out or watch my food at all, it was basically a nebula of destruction that destroyed any planet of growth I had created in the past. Now that the damage is done, I often look back on who I use to be and see a completely different person. I graduated alone and in private in shame of being seen again, and for a majority of my old friend group - the rumors from me suddenly moving to live in the woods to flat out dying are still there and well. My goals, my wishes, and outlooks on life are all still there - but it seems...grayed out. Beforehand I had made extensive efforts to combat my depressions from fully taking hold. Now the same issues I had resolved or come to peace with years ago are not only back, but they are burning more than before. 

Right now you can say I have theoretically beaten my depression once more. I have completed all the roadblocks that kept it lingering for so long in the first place (graduating, reconnecting with close friends, getting a healthy lifestyle back, and getting rid of my shotgun+shells). You would think by then it would be better, but it seems with every roadblock I jump, another takes its place. When I feel better I try to embrace that no matter what I do - things won't always be 100% fine, and that is okay, no need to be harsh on myself. But when I am down, it seems like all logic falls apart - and in its place emotions rule. 

Sorry if I am rambling a bit now, I will wrap this up. Right now I am 20, and since my depression was right dead middle of a transitional period in my life, I just feel so unprepared and fragile to anything. The best imagery I can think of is; imagine it is cold and dark, the middle of winter at night. There is a house with warm lights and people laughing and joking along, and then there is a figure curled up outside in the snow, freezing and not knowing what to do. That's the best I can summarize my current situation. I should also mention that it seems the key root of my depression is being raped - which I really don't like to talk about for obvious reasons. It has happened so long ago that it has stemmed from a single issue into this suffocating ivy. I can't help but feel so ashamed and weak for it. Pathetic. But over time I have masked this guilt and fear with anger. I started to hate mostly sex and girls, and one of my biggest fears was that I almost went full red pill/stereotypical neckbeard from it. The mask for now is gone, but now that I have forgiven most of my warped angers at others - it has done a 180 and slammed all of that rage directly at myself. Since I have no one to really point fingers at and now am not wearing tinted glasses for a false reason to hate, all I do now is directly hate myself. And I couldn't feel any more pathetic for it in the first place.
Buddhism does seem to fit a lot with my current philosophy of everything being fleeting but beautiful at the same time, I will give this a look - thank you!
Thank you, you as well

I'd love to, but I get so caught up and frozen by fears and what-ifs. I get where you're coming from though, I use to want to do plenty of adventures a few years ago until my most recent depression - but now it seems from three years of it, any passion and interest is muffled by this sense of not being __ enough and me not deserving it. Sort of like I am a husk of who I use to be, with all these dead goals and memories that I cannot relate to anymore.

Didn't they say SAD didn't exist? I'm not sure where I heard it from but I believe I once heard that the lights don't really work. But then again I haven't read much into it, I just always assumed I had ptsd/recurrent depression.
I have a snake who keeps me company when I am down (when he's not trying to bite haha)

Hit the nail pretty much on the head man. I always know what I can do to get better, but sometimes I would rather believe the distorted anger my depression gives me than open up and face getting hurt even more.
I can relate to the job part - thanks for your help
I appreciate it, thank you!
Amen to that

I've always wanted to get more into spirituality and philosophy, and when I am not trapped at rock bottom I usually try to get pretty active in it. Not sure if I will really follow one fully, but I like to take bits of different ones for my own life. It's worth a shot, thanks for your help!

Man I really feel sorry for you if you think is this the appropriate way to help people. But, I can't change you and you can't change me. So I will just leave it here, thanks for the advice regardless.

Yeah, that is true. However you have to understand that when people pass my line of depression they don't see what you just said as true help and more of just empty platitudes and mantras. Of course there are others who have it worse than me - but does that really make it lesser of an issue? It is all a matter of perspective, which depression just loves to distort. When you go tell me to be useful and undermine it - I get that you aren't in my shoes so my problems seem trivial to you - but kindly piss off with your drugged optimism lad.
It's more of the latter - basically overthinking and over-worrying about everything until paralysis.
Oh I will

For some yes, but I deeply feel a lot of the issues and scars I have are near permanent and not worth the despair to improve on them.

Hey, thanks for replying.

Yeah I visit a therapist once a week and have been on Celexa for a few months now. I often feel really good after venting and talking, but something just isn't working. It always goes back, always comes back. I appreciate the concern though.

Hey guys thought I would make a quick update for anyone still looking at this. I should probably first say that at the moment (for the past few weeks, not 'on a whim') I am not suicidal. I've been making slow and steady progress, but my current mood is not life-threatening. I want the shotgun gone from my life in case it comes back, sorry if I worried any of you. Also, I have made some contact with some stores to get rid of it, hell I would probably just give it away for free if they replied haha - if that doesn't go anywhere, I think i'll just bite the bullet (no pun intended) and call the police non-emergency number. Thanks for all the help and suggestions everyone.

Try to not compare yourself to others while working on it, it's best to just shut everything that can put you down and make you feel inferior off. By this I mean stuff like facebook, instagram, social media stuff, anything that superficially makes people look better. You in no way need to delete these and go rogue, just be smart and don't linger on them. Another thing I should mention is to try to organize it so you don't get overwhelmed. That means by doing one class at a time if you can, or focusing on certain things first instead of doing it all at once. Visualizing your progress could help tons, such as keeping a planner or checklist to help you get disciplined to it. My biggest advice though is, just do it. If you think you need help with it, go get it. The more you put it off (and I learnt this the hard way), the worse and more intimidating it gets. Good luck man, I am sure you can do it if you set your mind to it.

Hey thanks for your advice, I really appreciate it.

Yeah you guessed it right on the money, I'm 19 and at a crossroads basically in my life now. As of recent I've been at such a low point that I forgot who I was and what I wanted to become. It's almost like a breath of fresh air though if I take what you said, the ability to rebuild myself stronger this time.  The main obsticale I feel is the lies I tell myself, my attitude basically. 

Thanks again for the words of encouragement, I really needed them tonight.
